description: Document the new Supabase persistence: update .env.example and the README's 'Environment variables', 'Deployment (Vercel)', and 'Persistence caveat' sections to reflect that persistence is now durable via Supabase when configured, and still falls back to in-memory when unconfigured. Depends on FEAT-002 being implemented (docs describe the shipped behavior).
steps: Update `.env.example`: add `SUPABASE_URL=https://yuukqpmxaxsqewpgjlbu.supabase.co` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=` (left blank) with a comment that the service_role key is a SECRET pasted from Supabase dashboard -> Project Settings -> API -> service_role key, must NEVER be exposed to the client or committed, and that when either var is empty the app falls back to the in-memory store so build/tests/dev stay keyless. Do NOT add NEXT_PUBLIC_* client vars (all DB access is server-side).

Update README 'Environment variables' table: add rows for SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (Required: No for keyless dev/CI, but required for durable production persistence), describing the fallback-to-in-memory behavior when unset.

Update README 'Deployment (Vercel)' section: add a step to set SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY in Project Settings -> Environment Variables (Production/Preview), noting the service_role key is secret and bypasses RLS, and that without them the app runs on the non-durable in-memory store.

Update the README 'Persistence caveat' text (and the 'Production persistence' note in the Deployment section, and the in-scope/assumptions/roadmap mentions if they still say persistence is in-memory-only): explain that persistence is now durable via hosted Supabase Postgres when SUPABASE_URL + SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY are set (behind the unchanged BookStore/UserStore/ReviewStore interfaces), and the in-memory store remains the automatic keyless fallback for local dev / CI / preview. Note that the app manages its own cookie/JWT auth (not Supabase Auth) and the server uses the service_role key which bypasses the tables' enabled-but-policy-less RLS.

Do not overstate: the schema/migration is managed on the hosted DB; the README should not instruct the reader to run migrations from this repo (there is no migration tooling here). Keep wording accurate to what the code does.
acceptance_criteria: .env.example documents SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY with the secret warning and keyless-fallback note; no NEXT_PUBLIC_* vars added.

README Environment variables table, Deployment (Vercel) section, and Persistence caveat text all reflect durable Supabase persistence with in-memory fallback and are internally consistent (no lingering claim that persistence is in-memory only).
No secret key value is written into any file.
Keyless `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` still pass (docs-only change should not affect them).
verification: source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22 && npm run lint
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22 && npm run build
findings: Docs-only change. Updated .env.example (added SUPABASE_URL example value + blank SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY with secret/RLS warning and keyless-fallback note; no NEXT_PUBLIC_* vars). Updated README: Architecture store bullet, Environment variables table (two new rows + footnote), Persistence text, review-store line, Deployment (Vercel) env-var step + Production persistence note (schema managed on hosted DB, no migration tooling here), and MVP in-scope/assumptions/roadmap lines to reflect durable-Supabase-with-in-memory-fallback consistently. No secret value written anywhere. Verified keyless: npm run lint (0), npm test (93 passed / 16 files), npm run build (success).
